messages:
incident-bot: Paging @sre_oncall — automated alert: Canary v3 rollout 2026-03-14-22:03 triggered p99 latency > SLO on streaming endpoints (region us-west-2).

incident-bot: Metrics snapshot: p95=620ms (baseline 220ms), p99=5.6s (baseline 1.8s), error-rate spike +0.6%. Detected starting at 22:03:12 UTC.

sre_oncall: On it. I'm attaching to the call now — joining zoom. Quickly: which route?

maria: Looks like /v1/chat/stream on canary pool -> model: redwood-v3-small-quant. Traces show increased backend write time and stalled frames.

kev: I see the same in dashboards — the canary got ~10% traffic shift at 22:03 per rollout policy. p50 fine, but tail balloons. Could be kv-cache eviction pattern or kernel path for longer contexts.

ryan: Deploy bot posted rollout event:
```
deploy-bot: rollout started id=rl-20260314-57 status=progress traffic=10% -> redwood-v3-small-quant
```

support_jenna: Customer-impact reports: 2 customers opened tickets complaining about slow streaming updates and partial responses. Not yet major error counts.

sre_oncall: Ok triage plan: 1) Pin traffic -> reduce canary to 0% (immediate rollback if needed). 2) Check node metrics (IO, CPU, GPU util). 3) Look for model-specific tail logs.

maria: Running `redwoodctl rollouts patch rl-20260314-57 --traffic=0` now.

deploy-bot: Command accepted: updating traffic -> new allocation: canary 0% (rolling).

kev: Node metrics: a subset of canary hosts show sporadic high host_io_wait and process-level latency spikes. No OOMs. GPU util is normal ~25%.

ryan: I pulled a stacktrace from stream worker: `WriteTimeoutError: write to client socket exceeded 3000ms` repeated; seems worker backpressure when KV lookups miss.

maria: Rolling traffic down completed. Monitoring: p99 dropping from 5.6s -> 2.0s within 30s.

sre_oncall: Good. Keep rollback in flight until p99 stabilizes to <1.9s and errors normalize.

support_jenna: Updated ticket queue and posted temporary status message to affected customers: "We're aware of degraded streaming latency in US-West, reducing canary traffic and investigating. No data loss." :voice_off:

kev: Quick post-mortem note: suspect quantized weights + a fallback kernel path causing pathological memory access pattern leading to KV cache thrash under streaming prefix workloads. Only seen at tail when session lengths > 1024.

maria: We should also check model variant mapping — rollout used redwood-v3-small-quant:layerfused which we recently promoted. There was a perf guard but not a long tail test.

ryan: I recommend aborting this variant for production until we can repro locally. Opened issue INF-2337.

sre_oncall: Agreed. Action items: 
- rollback complete (maria)
- open INF ticket (ryan)
- capture flame graphs and KV hit/miss for affected hosts (kev)
- add synthetic tail test for session>1024 (maria + eng-ml)

maria: Rollback confirmed finished. p99 is now 420ms and p95 210ms. Error rates back to baseline.

deploy-bot: rollout rl-20260314-57 status=aborted by policy -> traffic set to 0; previous stable model restored.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV3: partial degradation, mitigated. Paging cleared for on-call.

support_jenna: Notifying customers that service has returned to normal and teams are investigating root cause.

sre_oncall: Handing off to @kev for follow-up deep dive; I'll be on-call for another 20m then handoff to night person. Key notes: canary traffic at 10% triggered tail > SLO for streaming route on quantized variant. Rollback to stable restored SLO.

kev: Acknowledged. I'll collect kv-cache metrics, kernel usage, and repro logs. Will sync with eng-ml tomorrow morning for model-level fixes.

maria: Adding replay job to reproduce with session lengths 800-1600 and cold cache. Kickoff id=job-20260314-tailtest.

ryan: INF-2337 created: "v3-small-quant tail latency regression on streaming; possible kv/cache thrash." Assigned to eng-ml.

support_jenna: Marking incident resolved for customers; monitoring for 2h.

sre_oncall: Closing thread here. If p99 creeps back up, re-paging. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
